items.summary: The Iran SNSC determination on the Hormuz re-closure closes Wednesday evening unannounced — Day 13 of contested compliance, seven full days since Majlis ratification confirmed the SNSC as the formal decision node, and six days since the IRGC cargo ship strike (June 26) has gone without SNSC acknowledgment, attribution, or disciplinary framing. No announcement was issued Tuesday or Wednesday. The re-closure remains formally operative. Physical Hormuz traffic continues to build through the CENTCOM corridor, with Kpler AIS data reflecting continued commercial vessel movement advancing from the June 24 +105% day-over-day baseline. Approximately 80 mines remain in the central channel, constraining all transit to CENTCOM-escorted routes. Lloyd's war-risk premiums hold at 3-8% of vessel value versus 0.25% pre-conflict. The Lloyd's normalization gate — the upstream requirement for the full 118-tanker backlog release — continues to require a formal SNSC position change that has not been issued. WTI crude is trading in the approximately $69-70 range through Wednesday — Day 11 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor — as physical traffic building (supply-positive) and Lebanon risk premium from Hezbollah's Day 4 non-compliance (potential re-escalation) continue to partially offset each other. The $65-70 range is establishing as the equilibrium for a 'partial reopening without formal SNSC' scenario. The 60-day oil sanctions waiver (through approximately August 18) provides six additional weeks of structural time buffer — there is no deadline forcing SNSC resolution before mid-August, which distinguishes the current period from the pre-MOU ultimatum pressure environment. Iran's Foreign Minister continues to characterize Swiss technical framework negotiations as producing 'no tangible progress' on uranium enrichment levels and HEU stockpile disposition. The SNSC's Day 13 silence creates a structurally paradoxical situation: the announcement is simultaneously less urgent (markets partially accepting physical transit as normalization proxy) and more necessary (Lloyd's formal gate remains closed; 118 tankers commercially stranded). Lebanon advances to Hour ~220+ through Wednesday evening without a formal void declaration. The Hezbollah non-compliance posture established by Naim Qassem's June 28 'null and void' rejection of the Rubio framework is now Day 4 operative. The ceasefire technically holds. Four consecutive days of Hezbollah political non-compliance without military escalation is the strongest post-rejection durability signal of the ceasefire period — the pattern supports the analytic read that the 'null and void' characterization remains political positioning rather than operational prelude. IDF drone activity in southern Lebanon continued Tuesday and Wednesday — Israeli presence in the 570 km² buffer zone that Netanyahu has explicitly stated will be held 'as long as necessary.' IMO 118-tanker convoy framework remains paused (Day 6 post-IRGC strike). Oregon pump prices approximately $5.25/gallon; national approximately $4.48/gallon.

items.summary: Russia's domestic fuel supply is under meaningful strain from Ukrainian long-range drone and missile strike campaigns against Russian oil refinery infrastructure — a strategic escalation in Ukraine's economic warfare approach that has moved beyond targeting military assets to disrupting domestic Russian supply chains. Putin publicly acknowledged fuel shortages, a notable admission that reflects the severity of domestic supply chain disruption: Russian state media rarely permits public acknowledgment of infrastructure damage from the conflict. Reports of physical altercations at Russian gas stations document the consumer-level impact of the refinery strike cascade — regional gasoline and diesel distribution is experiencing shortages with no immediate restoration timeline. Ukrainian targeting of Russian oil infrastructure has accelerated as a deliberate strategy to impose war economy costs. The domestic supply disruption has direct implications for Russian military logistics: fuel supply chains supporting front-line operations in Zaporizhzhia and Kupyansk corridors draw from the same domestic distribution network under attack; the Crimea fuel restriction emergency measures (ongoing since prior Ukrainian infrastructure strikes) are now compounded by the broader domestic distribution pressure. This development is the most significant Ukraine theater economic warfare milestone of the brief cycle. The broader Russian military escalation trajectory continues: 74 ballistic missiles per month, 75,000+ guided glide bombs projected for 2026. North Korea: Choe Hyon destroyer advances to Day 8 of Kim Jong Un's nuclear navy program without new provocations. PRC: 46-company ban advances to Day 4 of operational effect; Chinese Coast Guard east-of-Taiwan patrol pattern reaches Day 32. Peru ONPE: Day 27 of the 50.10%/49.90% working count; full official certification expected early July — within the current brief window. items.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill takes legal effect today, July 1, 2026. Medicaid work requirements and per-capita block grant conversion are operative as of today: states must begin enforcing work requirements for non-elderly, non-pregnant, non-disabled adult Medicaid enrollees or risk per-capita cap penalties. The state implementation readiness gap is the primary near-term OBBB risk surface — state Medicaid agencies had limited advance notice of the final text finalized through the 218-214 House vote, and several major states with complex Medicaid populations (Oregon approximately 1.4 million enrollees; Washington approximately 2.2 million) are in early-stage implementation preparation. CMS guidance on enforcement grace periods or federal waiver application frameworks is the primary resolution mechanism for the readiness gap. SALT deduction cap modification, top individual income tax rate reduction (retroactive to January 1, 2026), border security supplemental appropriations release, and energy production incentives are simultaneously effective. Washington state's new 2026 legislative session laws also took effect today — tax provisions, expanded benefits, rural data center guidelines, and healthcare licensing changes — adding to the July 1 simultaneous implementation load. Watson v. RNC introduces a new economic uncertainty thread with ongoing state fiscal implications: the ruling requires Oregon, Washington, California, Nevada, and other grace-period states to overhaul election administration infrastructure within five months at material state budget cost. Section 232 tariff enforcement on steel, aluminum, and copper at 50% advances to Day 30 — five full weeks operative. USTR de minimis proposed rules comment period closes July 6 (this Sunday) with the public hearing scheduled July 7. FERC large-load show-cause orders advance to Day 15; AI data center pathway explanation deadline at T-15 (~July 18) — the response window is in its final two weeks. Amazon Washington State WARN (2,198 positions; 30,000 total corporate layoffs since October 2025) and Bungie/Sony Bellevue (292 layoffs) continue as the structural PNW tech-labor bifurcation backdrop.

items.summary: The Tucannon Fire in southeastern Washington enters Day 4 of the East Cascades onset period with an estimated acreage of approximately 25,000+ acres — growth from the 15,000 acres reported at June 29 evening, driven by record-setting 100-hour fuel dryness for this calendar date per the Northwest Coordination Center, persistent Red Flag conditions in southeastern Washington, and continued air attack constraints from smoke column development during peak afternoon burning windows. Level 3 (Go Now) evacuation orders remain active in Garfield County's Pomeroy area corridor. A second PNW heat wave is arriving this week — less than 10 days after the first heat wave of summer — with AccuWeather projecting record-challenging temperatures in Seattle and Portland and NOAA's July outlook confirming above-normal temperatures sustained throughout the month. The second heat wave will intensify Tucannon's fuel dryness environment and extend Red Flag conditions into the July 4 weekend, when human ignition risk (fireworks, holiday activity) compounds the meteorological fire environment. A new fire incident emerged near Winthrop in Okanogan County, northwestern Washington — a rapidly growing ignition that prompted full-town evacuation of Winthrop before partial stabilization allowed partial evacuation order downgrade Wednesday. The Winthrop/Okanogan incident is the East Cascades onset period's second geographic front. The partial evacuation lifting represents a partial positive; the fire remains active and requires continued suppression resources, adding to the regional commitment from Tucannon. Tule Road (Toppenish/Yakima County, approximately 24,087 acres) has reached approximately 100% containment, releasing resources for Tucannon. Juniper Dunes (Grant County) is approaching full containment. All other prior fires (Kartar, Peterson, Twin Sisters, Upriver) remain at 100% containment. The resource conversion from prior containment reserve to active simultaneous commitment on Tucannon and Winthrop/Okanogan has advanced significantly: the July-September primary risk window now opens with a substantially reduced suppression resource buffer. NIFC Preparedness Level 3 advances to Day 15. BPA grid stable. NSF Newport OR operational.

The simultaneous IRGC-Hezbollah dual-elevated posture is the brief cycle's most concentrated critical infrastructure cyber threat moment. items.summary: The Supreme Court issued a Voting Rights Act ruling — announced within the brief cycle since the June 29 evening report — that immediately enabled Florida Republicans to approve an aggressively gerrymandered congressional district map projected to net the GOP approximately four additional House seats in November 2026. The VRA ruling's downstream consequence materialized within hours: Florida's Republican-controlled legislature approved the new map, demonstrating the high-velocity state exploitation pattern also seen with Watson v. RNC. The combined electoral disruption landscape now carries three concurrent tracks heading into November 2026 midterms five months out: (1) Watson v. RNC — mail ballot grace periods eliminated in all 50 states; Oregon, Washington, California, Nevada, and others must overhaul election administration within five months; (2) Trump mail-in voting EO — executive action further restricting mail voting beyond Watson's statutory holding; court challenges filed June 29 advancing through federal circuit review; (3) VRA ruling — congressional map gerrymandering enabled in affected states; Florida's immediate exploitation projects a multi-seat net GOP gain; other states likely to follow. Court challenges to all three tracks are active. The combined effect is the most significant pre-midterm electoral landscape disruption since Dobbs (2022). Chief Justice Roberts' term-defining split alignment — with the liberal bloc on constitutional immigration (Trump v. Barbara) but with the conservative majority on federal election preemption (Watson) — has now been extended by the VRA ruling into a pattern: the Court is expanding statutory federal preemption and state redistricting authority while maintaining constitutional rights floors. The OBBB takes legal effect today, July 1. Medicaid work requirements and per-capita block grant conversion are operative. State implementation readiness gap is the primary near-term domestic risk surface: state Medicaid agencies had limited advance notice of the final text. CMS enforcement grace period or waiver application guidance is the resolution mechanism. The legislative track is fully resolved; implementation is the new uncertainty surface. Acting DNI Day 42 — eighth consecutive week without Senate-confirmed IC leadership at the brief cycle's most complex simultaneous domestic threat convergence.

items.summary: The Pacific Northwest enters July 1 evening with compounding wildfire, heat, and seismic developments. The Tucannon Fire has grown to an estimated 25,000+ acres from 15,000 acres as of June 29 evening — driven by record-setting 100-hour fuel dryness for this calendar date (confirmed by NW Coordination Center by fire behavior), persistent Red Flag conditions in southeastern Washington, and limited air attack effectiveness during peak burning windows due to smoke column development. Level 3 evacuation orders remain active in Garfield County's Pomeroy area. A second PNW heat wave is arriving this week — less than 10 days after the first heat wave of summer — with AccuWeather projecting record-challenging temperatures in Seattle and Portland; NOAA's July outlook confirms above-normal temperatures and sustained drought conditions throughout the month. The second heat wave will intensify Tucannon's fuel dryness environment and extend Red Flag conditions into the July 4 weekend, when human ignition risk (fireworks, recreation, agricultural) compounds the meteorological fire environment into the most elevated ignition-risk period of the onset season. A new fire near Winthrop in Okanogan County prompted full-town evacuation before partial stabilization allowed partial evacuation order downgrade Wednesday — a partial positive; the fire remains active and is the onset period's second geographic suppression commitment. An M5.5 earthquake struck approximately 4:35 a.m. Monday under the Pacific Ocean near the Oregon coast. No significant damage or tsunami warnings were reported. The event underscores the ongoing Cascadia Subduction Zone seismic hazard context — the brief's structural long-horizon risk backdrop. Lake Chelan (Chelan County) is closed to boaters following a significant influx of logs, ash, and sediment washed in from the 2024 Pioneer Fire burn scar — a secondary disaster pattern from prior wildfire seasons disrupting the lake's summer recreational economy at peak season. Tule Road (approximately 24,087 acres) reached approximately 100% containment, releasing resources for Tucannon. Juniper Dunes is near-full containment. BPA grid stable. NSF Newport OR operational. NIFC PL3 Day 15. Oregon EO 26-10 Day 18.

analyst_summary: July 1, 2026 evening closes at Vibe 4 — holding for the sixth consecutive session since Friday June 26, now through the OBBB's implementation day and the emergence of the VRA ruling's downstream electoral consequences. The brief cycle's thread composition has shifted substantially over the past 48 hours without the aggregate risk level moving: OBBB implementation is the structural positive — five weeks of legislative uncertainty fully resolved, now operative law; VRA ruling plus Watson v. RNC plus Trump mail EO constitutes the three-track election disruption structural new negative; and the Hormuz-Lebanon-Tucannon triple continues as the load-bearing uncertainty frame unchanged in character since Friday. The July 1 convergence is distinct from Monday's SCOTUS convergence: where June 29 delivered discrete resolution events (opinions issued, OBBB signed, measles window closed), July 1 delivers simultaneous implementation activations against a backdrop of continuing escalation in two asymmetric domains — wildfire and election administration disruption. The SCOTUS VRA ruling's high-velocity downstream exploitation — Florida Republicans approving a gerrymander projecting +4 GOP House seats within hours — demonstrates the pattern established by Watson v. RNC: election law rulings in this cycle are being exploited in real time, far ahead of court challenge resolution windows. The combined three-track disruption (Watson ballot restrictions, Trump mail EO, VRA gerrymander) is operating simultaneously with five months to November 2026 — the most consequential simultaneous pre-midterm disruption since Dobbs. The Hormuz situation on Day 13 has reached a novel structural equilibrium: markets have partially priced in the physical traffic building as supply-positive, WTI has stabilized in the $65-70 range, and the 60-day sanctions waiver provides six weeks of time buffer that allows the SNSC to maintain silence without a forced resolution event. The Lloyd's gate formally remains closed, and 118 tankers remain commercially stranded — but the market's willingness to partially accept a 'normalization without formal announcement' narrative has compressed the front-running gap from its June 29 maximum. Lebanon's fragile hold at Hour ~220+ with Hezbollah's Day 4 political rejection in place without military escalation is the ceasefire's strongest post-rejection durability signal — four days of political non-compliance without operational resumption increasingly reads as positioning rather than prelude. The Russia domestic fuel crisis is the week's most significant geopolitical signal: Putin-acknowledged refinery strike cascade producing domestic shortages and gas station altercations represents the most impactful Ukrainian economic warfare outcome since the conflict's expansion. On infrastructure: the second heat wave arriving this week, Tucannon's estimated growth to 25,000+ acres, the new Winthrop/Okanogan ignition, and the July 4 holiday weekend human ignition overlay collectively define the most demanding simultaneous fire risk period of the onset season. The Oregon renewable energy construction deadline this Friday July 4 adds a closing-window implementation pressure partially obscured by the holiday. Tomorrow's June employment report (BLS, July 2) and Sunday's SpaceX Nasdaq-100 entry (July 6) are the week's dominant economic events, with the jobs report as the near-term FOMC October hike pivot and SpaceX's inclusion as the structural market rebalancing event.
